title: Treat the selected record as provenance in 99 replay checks (no new κ)
body:
## What changes

99 `verify.py` files in research packages I authored. No other file changes.

- The live check `selected = json.loads(... certificates/selected-result.json ...)` plus `kappa == "<old value>"` is removed. A one-line comment replaces it.
- In 4 files the pin loop also hashed `usage: "provenance"` rows against the working tree. Those files now skip non-`input` rows, matching the other 95.

Results, `RESULT.json`, `SOURCES.json`, `VERIFY.json`, pins and evidence are all unchanged.

## Why

[`docs/research/research-package-guide.md`](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/main/docs/research/research-package-guide.md) says the selected record is historical provenance, "so future priority changes do not invalidate a package". Each of these packages already pins `certificates/selected-result.json` as `usage: "provenance"`, and `scripts/research_package.py` checks it at `base_commit` through Git. The verifiers asserted the live κ anyway, so every frontier change broke them. On main 1ec111997:

- 63 assert `60403/20000000` and broke at the #4610 admission.
- 34 had already failed since the `23/10000` era.
- 2 assert an even older value, `836330098538459/500000000000000000`.

Re-pinning to the new κ would break again at the next frontier change, so this removes the live dependency instead.

## Validation

On this branch (main 1ec111997 + this commit), CPython 3.12:

- `python3.12 -I -B <package>/verify.py`: **99/99 pass**. All 99 failed before this change.
- `python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package <package> --check-only`: 99/99 `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`. This includes the base-commit provenance check of the selected record.

CI will replay all 99 packages because they changed. The heaviest is `two-three-cycle-additivity`, with a 600 s budget. The total declared budget is 8,280 s.

## Scope

This is replay maintenance only. No mathematical claim, κ or frontier changes. Other contributors' packages with the same pattern are not touched.
